probability.label: Confident · 98%
probability.scope: These percentages assess each existing child-to-William profile pair from the combined named household, locality and compatible generation; they are subjective, not measured frequencies. The will proves the stated father roles through a checked transcription, not the children’s exact birthdays, later migrations, spouses or descendants. probability.basis: The named daughter Sophia matches the youngest Currituck child account within the complete sibling set. Her estimated age of four at the will fits, but neither that exact birth nor later marriage is established by it. William Glasgow’s Currituck will, dated 14 October 1805 and recorded 22 January 1806, names wife Sarah, sons Caleb, Isaac, Samuel and John C., and daughters Ruth, Love Bright and Sophia. Its land divisions and household bequests identify one specific family. The named wife and all seven child names strongly identify the maintained William-357 family, with John C. compatible with John Cooper and Love now recorded under Bright; this conjunction outweighs the unsourced August death claim. The published transcription is by Judy Merrell Brickhouse, citing Currituck County Will Book 2, pp.279–280. The manuscript was not inspected. The will also transfers an enslaved boy; that clause does not add a biological family relationship.
